title: Sadie Gray Mays (1900-1969) - NewsBreak
text:
By BlackPast Site Admin ,
1 days ago Photo courtesy of the archives held at the Auburn Avenue Research Library on African American History and Culture, Atlanta, GA. Mrs. Sadie Gray Mays was a pioneering social worker, higher education administrator, federal agency leader, and community institutional builder who served for 27 years as the First Lady of Morehouse College. Born to a farming family in Gray, Georgia, Mrs. Mays forged an independent career in social casework and university instruction before stepping into administrative leadership alongside her husband, Dr. Benjamin E. Mays. Over their 43-year partnership, she dedicated her administrative talents and uncompensated labor toward the institutional development of Morehouse College, pioneering holistic student retention strategies and pastoral counseling. Beyond her university tenure, Mrs. Mays was a prominent catalyst within Black women’s civic welfare networks in Atlanta and nationwide, culminating in her leadership as President of the Board of Directors for the Happy Haven Nursing Home.
